How to Program an NES Game in C

summary.title: How to Program an NES game in C (nesdoug)
summary.one_liner: Learn how to write NES games in C using the cc65 compiler and the neslib library, through a series of tutorials on nesdoug.com.
takeaways: NES games can be written in C using the cc65 toolchain instead of pure assembly.
The site's tutorial series covers topics such as controllers and sprite collisions, and a basic platformer.
The neslib library is used in the examples; the author mentions an updated version compatible with newer cc65 releases.
All tutorial code is hosted on GitHub, according to the site.
The page also links to a related SNES tool, SuperFamiconv, and a Russian translation of the tutorial.
summary.summary: This is the home page of a tutorial series by nesdoug on programming the NES in C with the cc65 compiler. The page lists tutorial entries such as "Controllers (and sprite collisions)" and links to the complete code on GitHub. Its comments section adds context: neslib example code updates for newer cc65 versions, a note that asm6 is not compatible with cc65, and a mention of the SuperFamiconv tool for SNES work. The page text does not show the individual lessons in detail.
